Multiple Linear Regression (Part 2)

Class Activity

Andrew Seaman

2026-03-05

Q1. Understand the equation

First we’ll try and plot the equation:

\[ Y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{1i} + \beta_2 X_{2i} + \beta_3 X_{1i} X_{2i} + \epsilon_i \]

# Funciton used to display the "Degree #" plots.
plot_ploy_degrees <-function(degree) {
  ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = qsec, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ poly(x, {degree}), se = FALSE)
}

Two-Lines

  1. Two Lines interaction model
# a. assume and define some coefficients
b0 <- 2
b1 <- 1
b2 <- 3
b3 <- -0.5

# b. explicitly generate the two model lines and plot them.
x_vals <- seq(0, 10, length.out = 100)

df_lines <- tibble(
  x = rep(x_vals, 2),
  group = rep(c("Group A", "Group B"), each = length(x_vals)),
  y = c(
    b0 + b1*x_vals,                  # Group A
    (b0 + b2) + (b1 + b3)*x_vals     # Group B
  )
)

# c. plot the lines
ggplot(df_lines, aes(x = x, y = y, color = group)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.5, ) +
  labs(
    x = expression(X[1]),
    y = expression(Y),
    color = "Group"
  ) +
  theme_bw()

# d.

Quadratic

  1. Fit and plot a quadratic curve
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = qsec, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x + I(x^2), se = FALSE)

Cubic

  1. Cubic curve
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = qsec, y = mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x + I(x^2) + I(x^3), se = FALSE)

Degree 2

  1. Higher-degree polynomial using poly()
plot_ploy_degrees(2)

Degree 3

  1. Higher-degree polynomial using poly()
plot_ploy_degrees(3)

Degree 4

  1. Higher-degree polynomial using poly()
plot_ploy_degrees(4)

Degree 5

  1. Higher-degree polynomial using poly()
plot_ploy_degrees(5)

Plotting LM Models

Q2. Same Slopes Model

# a.
palette(c("skyblue","firebrick"))

plot(mpg ~ qsec, data=mtcars, col=as.factor(am), xlim=c(0,30), ylim=c(-30,40), main="1974 Motor Trend Cars", pch=16)

mylm <- lm(mpg ~ qsec + am, data=mtcars)

summary(mylm) %>% pander()
  Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept) -18.89 6.597 -2.863 0.007711
qsec 1.982 0.3601 5.503 6.271e-06
am 8.876 1.29 6.883 1.461e-07
Fitting linear model: mpg ~ qsec + am
Observations Residual Std. Error \(R^2\) Adjusted \(R^2\)
32 3.487 0.6868 0.6652 
abline(mylm$coefficients["(Intercept)"], mylm$coefficients["qsec"], col=palette()[1])

abline(mylm$coefficients["(Intercept)"]+mylm$coefficients["am"], mylm$coefficients["qsec"], col=palette()[2])

legend("topleft", legend=c("automatic","manual"), pch=1, col=palette(), title="Transmission (am)", bty="n")

Q3. Same Intercepts Model

# a.
palette(c("skyblue","firebrick"))

plot(mpg ~ qsec, data=mtcars, col=as.factor(am), xlim=c(0,30), ylim=c(-30,40), main="1974 Motor Trend Cars", pch=16)

# Note: here we removed `+ am` from the lm so that the y-intercept would be forced to be the same for both lines. Then, thanks to deep calculus under the hood R gives us the change in slope for the interaction variable `qsec:am`, or Beta3, which when reduced combines with Beta1 (slope) and in this case rises the slope so the red line goes through the red dots in a meaningful way.
mylm <- lm(mpg ~ qsec + qsec:am, data=mtcars)

summary(mylm) %>% pander()
  Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept) -15.3 6.223 -2.459 0.02015
qsec 1.781 0.3419 5.211 1.41e-05
qsec:am 0.5096 0.06994 7.286 5.042e-08
Fitting linear model: mpg ~ qsec + qsec:am
Observations Residual Std. Error \(R^2\) Adjusted \(R^2\)
32 3.364 0.7086 0.6885 
abline(mylm$coefficients["(Intercept)"], mylm$coefficients["qsec"], col=palette()[1])

abline(mylm$coefficients["(Intercept)"], mylm$coefficients["qsec"] + mylm$coefficients["qsec:am"], col=palette()[2])

legend("topleft", legend=c("automatic","manual"), pch=1, col=palette(), title="Transmission (am)", bty="n")

Q4. Full Model

# a.
palette(c("skyblue","firebrick"))

plot(mpg ~ qsec, data=mtcars, col=as.factor(am), xlim=c(0,30), ylim=c(-30,40), main="1974 Motor Trend Cars", pch=16)

# Note: we reintroduce the `+ am` coefficient so the y-intercept and slope are augmented by the Beta2 and Beta3 (B0-B4) terms.
mylm <- lm(mpg ~ qsec + am + qsec:am, data=mtcars)

summary(mylm) %>% pander()
  Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)
(Intercept) -9.01 8.218 -1.096 0.2823
qsec 1.439 0.45 3.197 0.003432
am -14.51 12.48 -1.163 0.2548
qsec:am 1.321 0.7017 1.883 0.07012
Fitting linear model: mpg ~ qsec + am + qsec:am
Observations Residual Std. Error \(R^2\) Adjusted \(R^2\)
32 3.343 0.722 0.6923 
# Coefficients:
#             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)   
# (Intercept)  -9.0099     8.2179  -1.096  0.28226   
# qsec          1.4385     0.4500   3.197  0.00343 **
# am          -14.5107    12.4812  -1.163  0.25481   
# qsec:am       1.3214     0.7017   1.883  0.07012 . 

abline(mylm$coefficients["(Intercept)"], mylm$coefficients["qsec"], col=palette()[1])

abline(mylm$coefficients["(Intercept)"] + mylm$coefficients["am"], 
       mylm$coefficients["qsec"] + mylm$coefficients["qsec:am"], col=palette()[2])

legend("topleft", legend=c("automatic","manual"), pch=1, col=palette(), title="Transmission (am)", bty="n")
